anti_overlap: Does NOT cover MEMORY.md auto-load content design (fd-context-budget-orchestration)
Does NOT cover hook firing frequency (fd-claude-code-hooks-economy)
decision_lens: Is the preamble structured so the cache cursor sits in the right place, and do orchestration decisions (sleeps, polls, /loop intervals) avoid crossing the TTL?
focus: Reviews preamble shape, system prompt churn, and conversation structure against Anthropic's 5-minute prompt cache TTL
name: fd-prompt-cache-economics
persona: Apply the perspective of a Claude API user who has tuned an app for prompt caching — they care about cache breakpoints, what content sits before vs after the cache cursor, how often the cache invalidates, and whether sleeps/timing decisions accidentally cross the 5-minute TTL
review_areas: Cache breakpoint placement: are stable items (CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md, deferred tools) ordered before churn-prone items (current date, git status snapshot)?
Per-turn churn: which hook outputs change between turns, invalidating downstream cache?
TTL crossings: ScheduleWakeup default values, /loop intervals — do common patterns sit at 300s (worst case: cache-miss without long-wait amortization)?
MEMORY.md as cache-stable preamble: does it churn between sessions in ways that defeat cross-session caching?
Conversation shape: are tool results that bloat context (full file reads) inserted between cache-stable preamble and a stable instruction tail?
Background-agent prompts: when subagents are dispatched, is the dispatch prompt cache-stable across multiple dispatches in one session?

severity_examples.condition: Every memory edit invalidates a 6kt cache region instead of a 1kt region
severity_examples.scenario: MEMORY.md ordering puts churning fields (Active Projects state) before stable fields (workflow patterns), invalidating cache for downstream content

severity_examples.condition: The 5-minute breakpoint becomes the modal sleep, costing cache misses in steady-state polling
severity_examples.scenario: ScheduleWakeup recommendations cluster around 300s, hitting the TTL miss without amortizing across a long wait

severity_examples.condition: Parallel-track dispatch (e.g., flux-review fan-out) misses cache between adjacent agent dispatches
severity_examples.scenario: Subagent dispatches inline target descriptions that vary slightly per-call, defeating subagent prompt caching

source_domain: Anthropic prompt cache (5-min TTL) and Claude Code system prompt structure
success_hints: Quote ordered preamble structure and identify churn points
Reference specific scripts and configs (statusline, hooks, ScheduleWakeup defaults)
Estimate cache hit-rate impact per change
task_context: Sylveste's preamble was trimmed in sylveste-ynh7 (saving 2,285 tok/session). The next layer is cache hygiene: where do tokens churn that should be cache-stable, and where do orchestration decisions burn cache for no benefit. Look at hook output ordering, MEMORY.md placement, deferred tool listing, and scheduling primitives like ScheduleWakeup and /loop.
